content:
Recent public perception of Meta AI glasses has noticeably deteriorated—so much so that on today's US iPhone paid App Store chart, one of the top three spots has been taken by an app specifically designed to detect who nearby is wearing smart glasses.

The app's name leaves nothing to the imagination: Antizuck Smart Glasses Scanner, which claims to detect and alert you to who nearby is wearing Meta AI glasses.

Enough iPhone users are willing to spend US$3 to try this app that it now sits at number three on the US iPhone paid App Store chart—a remarkable achievement for a newly launched paid app.

We haven't tested this app ourselves, so we can't confirm whether it actually works; furthermore, even if it does detect AI glasses, what you should do once you've spotted someone wearing them remains very much unknown.

Smart glasses fitted with cameras are still fairly easy to spot in person these days, so you may well not need an app to help you keep an eye on who's wearing them.

That said, the message from the public is already crystal clear: many people feel deeply uncomfortable with the very idea of AI smart glasses, viewing them as a privacy issue. If Apple wants to enter the smart glasses fray next year, this undoubtedly represents a significant headwind.
